Yesterday, the US government announced an update to the list of prohibited foreign-made products, adding "advanced robotic devices" to the list. Today, a spokesperson for the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) confirmed that the ban also covers robotic vacuum cleaners.

The robotic vacuum ban affects Roomba, Roborock, and other well-known brands — but you can continue to use your existing products.

When the Trump administration announced a ban on "advanced robotic devices" entering the US yesterday, media attention focused on humanoid robots. But surveillance doesn't require legs — and neither does the FCC's robot ban. Katie Gorscak, the FCC's Director of Media Relations, confirmed to The Verge that the ban also applies to robotic vacuum cleaners. Roomba units already purchased are not affected, and approved models may continue to be imported and sold. However, the government claims that future foreign robots will pose national security risks, and even robotic vacuum companies have suddenly been required to commit to manufacturing in the United States.

The FCC considers advanced robotic devices to carry national security risks. Even seemingly harmless products — such as robotic vacuums, robotic lawn mowers, etc. — are equally covered.

Unless explicitly approved, or manufactured domestically in the United States, all such products are prohibited from being sold in the US.

This ban is particularly devastating to the robotic vacuum market, as mainstream brands like Roomba, Roborock, and Ecovacs are all Chinese-owned.

If you already own one of the products mentioned above, you can continue to use it as normal today; the FCC won't be showing up at your door to confiscate your robot vacuum.

However, depending on how the ban is ultimately enforced, the robotic vacuum market could see dramatic changes in the short term. If all of this sounds familiar, that's because the situation with the recent wireless router ban was almost identical.

Will you continue using your existing robotic vacuum? Why? Let us know in the comments.
